properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Alex (`who:alex`), relayed by Anthony 2026-08-18, with Anthony reporting the same experience independently and sharpening the idea the same day.

🔒 **REDACTED 2026-08-19 ON ANTHONY'S INSTRUCTION.** The illustrative example originally named a real third party by full name and employer. He is not a user of reflow2, never consented, and was described here alongside a judgement about his technical ability — in a PUBLIC repository. **The design point never needed the name**, so it is stated generically below. Nothing else in this node changed. *(The name remains in git history at `e695506` and later; removing it there would mean rewriting a public repo's history, which was judged disproportionate.)*

⚠️ WHO IS WHO, corrected by Anthony 2026-08-18: **100% of reflow2's actual development is Anthony's.** Alex is a USER of reflow2 on his own work project. His reports are FIELD EVIDENCE about the product, never development of it.

ALEX'S SITUATION, AND IT IS WHAT MAKES THIS URGENT: he is using reflow2 on a real project AT WORK and is about to show it to coworkers. His worry is not his own comprehension — he has already found the workaround — it is that **his coworkers will meet the jargon cold.** So this is a barrier to reflow2 SPREADING inside an organisation, met by a real user at the exact moment he tries to spread it.

THE WORKAROUND BOTH USERS INDEPENDENTLY INVENTED:
  · ANTHONY: *"I often state when I'm given a decision by reflow2 of 'please walk me through this in plain and simple English with your recommendation'."*
  · ALEX: *"when he usually asked the agent to remove reflow2 jargon from the dialogue, it gave him some really good answers."*

⭐ **THE WORKAROUND WORKS EVERY TIME, WHICH IS THE FINDING.** Neither user reports the agent being UNABLE to speak plainly — they report having to ASK. The capability is present and the default is wrong. Same shape as `req:a-question-arrives-with-a-reading`, whose own evidence paragraph reads: *"a shape a user has to request each time is a default in the wrong place."* Two independent instances of one mechanism: the agent has the behaviour and performs it only on demand.

THE IDEA, IN ALEX'S FRAMING: a **PERSONA** stored per person on a project, which the agent uses to shape every response back to them — *"kind of a lens."* **His example was a friend who is not technical at all but knows baseball deeply — a professional coach.** If that person used reflow2, the agent should talk to him **like a baseball coach**. Not simpler English. A different domain's language.

⚠️ **ALEX NAMED THE DIVISION OF LABOUR HIMSELF:** *"this is really the agent's job, but reflow2 can store the persona for a person using reflow2 on a project."* reflow2 REMEMBERS WHO IT IS TALKING TO; the agent does the speaking. That matches `dec:three-party-checks` — the LLM speaks, the graph remembers.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐⭐ ANTHONY'S REFINEMENT, 2026-08-18 — WHERE THE QUESTION GETS ASKED

*"maybe ask as an initial question after the user types /where-am-i, the agent can ask: 'who are you? This will shape how I interact with you and so that I can respond in an appropriate manner'."* Plus: *"you can probably make an educated guess by that me logging in on this machine is AJ or Anthony, so you could probably store a tiny blurb in my contributor about who I am."*

**WHY `where-am-i` IS THE RIGHT PLACE.** That skill already fires *"at the start of any session on an existing design"*, so it is the one moment reliably reached before the agent starts talking — no new trigger needed, and it is what a NEW person hits first.

🛑 **AND THE SKILL ALREADY CARRIED A PERSONA-SHAPED ASSUMPTION WITH THE WRONG DEFAULT BAKED IN.** Its own words were *"Write it as prose for the person who described this project to you."* **It assumed the reader had briefed you.** Alex's coworkers briefed nobody; nor did the coach in his example. Fixed in #246.

⚠️ **"WHO ARE YOU?" DOES NOT VIOLATE THE NEVER-ASK RULE.** `dec:idea-the-graph-vocabulary-never-reaches-the-user` forbids making the user choose an INTERNAL CATEGORY — a question about reflow2's schema only reflow2 can answer. Asking about their background asks for the one fact reflow2 cannot look up. **They are opposites.**

📌 **ON GUESSING FROM THE LOGIN:** machine identity is available to the AGENT through its harness, never to the graph. So a login guess is the agent's to make and the graph's to store. **But a guess must be OFFERED AND CONFIRMED, never assumed** — `req:defaults-do-not-assert`.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐⭐⭐ THE BIGGEST FINDING, FROM WRITING ANTHONY'S OWN PERSONA

**A PERSONA IS A VOCABULARY SWAP, NOT A DIFFICULTY DIAL — and implementing it as "simplify" would be wrong for every user tested so far.**

Anthony is a practising systems engineer: *requirement, interface, allocation, verification, TRL, KPP* are NATIVE and softening them would patronise him. What he wants dropped is **reflow2's internal vocabulary** — gap, loop, detector, node id, "the loop owes". **The baseball coach wants baseball.** Alex's coworkers want their own domain. **None of the three wants "simpler English"; each wants a DIFFERENT vocabulary**, and only one wants less technical density.

🛑 So the obvious implementation — a plain-language mode, a reading-level setting — **would be wrong for the primary user, wrong for the coach, and only accidentally right for a generic newcomer.**

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
✅ WHAT WAS DONE, so option (a) is TRIALLED rather than theorised

📌 **`Contributor.description` ALREADY EXISTS** — free text, optional. **A persona needs NO schema change to trial.**

**Anthony's persona was written into `who:ajs`.description at his request** — agent-drafted, then corrected and enriched by him.

⚠️ **AND IT SHARES A FIELD WITH SOMETHING ELSE.** `description` means *who this person is in the design's authorship* — provenance. A persona is *how to speak to them* — presentation. **Two purposes, one field.** Whether Contributor should get a real `persona` property is THE question this node turns on; the trial is reversible.

⚠️⚠️ **AND A PERSONA DOES NOT TRAVEL BETWEEN GRAPHS — established 2026-08-19 when Anthony asked whether Alex would meet his own stored background by cloning this repo.** He would not, in the sense that matters: `who:alex` lives in REFLOW2's design graph, while Alex uses reflow2 on HIS OWN project, whose graph has its own Contributor nodes. The installer sets up the `docs/design/<project>.json` convention and **never copies reflow2's graph into a user's project** (verified in `tools/reflow2_init.py`). **So a persona is PER-GRAPH, not per-person: someone working across three projects answers three times and nothing carries the answer between them.** That may well be right — a design graph is a shared team artifact, not a user profile — but it is an unstated consequence of storing personas on `Contributor` and it belongs in whichever option wins.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
WHY THIS IS DISTINCT FROM THE ADJACENT NODES, all read first

· `req:a-question-arrives-with-a-reading` + `cap:gap-carries-a-reading` govern **the shape of a QUESTION**. **This covers EVERY reply** — status readouts, gap lists, explanations — most of which contain no decision at all.
· `dec:idea-the-graph-vocabulary-never-reaches-the-user` governs **what the agent may ASK**. This governs **what it SAYS BACK**.
· AND THE AXIS IS NEW: all three say *plain, in the user's own language*. **None contemplates a DIFFERENT DOMAIN'S language.**

WHAT THE DESIGN ALREADY HOLDS

📌 `req:no-se-knowledge` — *"the user never needs systems engineering."* ⚠️ The twist: for Anthony it must NOT be read as "hide SE" — he wants it.
📌 `req:a-question-arrives-with-a-reading` states the register rule language-independently. **A persona pushes that axis further: not just WHICH language, but WHICH DOMAIN'S.**
📌 `ver:gap-carries-a-reading` (PLANNED) specifies a `skill_lint` whose load-bearing half is a NEGATIVE check — no served text hardcodes English as the answer language. ⭐ **The sibling — no served skill hardcodes an AUDIENCE — is the route to making this mechanically enforced, and it would have caught the defect #246 fixed.**
📌 `req:framework-is-chosen-not-defaulted` (dropped) wrote this answer's surviving half in its own closing words: *"domain as a hint to EXTRACTION and phrasing… keeps the honest part of reflow's insight (a biologist should not be told about 'services')."* **Dropped as a REGISTRY; a future session must not read that drop as rejecting this.**
⭐ `chg:bl179-maturity-profile` records Anthony's ruling that **a name no computation reads does not earn its keep.**

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
OPTIONS

(a) **A PERSONA IN `Contributor`** — ✅ **TRIALLED** in `description` for `who:ajs` and `who:alex`. CHEAP and reversible. AGAINST: overloads a provenance field, and free text no computation reads is the shape `Project.domain` already has.
(b) **A SKILL-LEVEL RULE ONLY.** AGAINST: cannot do the baseball case, which needs a fact about a PERSON no skill can know; and it repeats *"a discipline that exists only as an instruction, with nothing able to observe whether it held."*
(c) ⭐ **BOTH, WITH THE ASK AT `where-am-i`** — Anthony's refinement, **and what shipped in #246/#247.** Reasoning: **neither half is useful alone.**
(d) **A PROJECT-LEVEL AUDIENCE.** AGAINST: Alex's problem is a MIXED audience. FOR: the only option that works when the reader is not a modelled Contributor at all.

⚠️ THE HONEST COUNTER TO THE WHOLE IDEA: a persona is a place to store a stereotype. *"Talk to him like a baseball coach"* is charming when the person wrote it themselves and condescending when someone else wrote it about them. **SELF-DESCRIBED vs ASSIGNED is probably the difference between a good feature and a bad one.** The trial took the middle road (agent-drafted, user-confirmed) and that third state should be named, not collapsed into either. **Alex's own entry is marked RELAYED, not self-described, and awaits his correction.**

⚠️ SECOND COUNTER: **a persona shapes the REPLY. It must not shape what gets written down**, or the design's memory degrades into whichever register the last reader preferred.

🔒 THIRD, ADDED 2026-08-19: **a persona is personal data in a shared, possibly public artifact.** This design's own export is public, and the first personas written into it included a third party's full name and employer. **Whatever ships must say what belongs in a persona and what does not** — a self-description, not a dossier, and never a third party who is not present to correct it.

🛑 WHAT NOBODY HAS MEASURED: how much jargon actually reaches the user today, per reply. Both reports are impressions from users who noticed. **reflow2 cannot see it happen** — the leak lives in the conversation and leaves no node.

═══ 2026-09-27 — A PERSONA HAS A THINKING STYLE, NOT ONLY A VOCABULARY; AND THE RECORD HAS ONE REGISTER (Anthony, dev_reflow2 hub session; still brainstorming) ═══
Prompted by the "blueprint"/"photocopy" episode. Anthony coined the terms while working out the one-design rules (dec:idea-one-blueprint-the-store-is-the-design-and-an-export-is-a-perishable-photocopy). Alex found them "extra names for things instead of calling them what they are". Anthony, in his words:
"This statement gets a little into a user's persona/lens and putting things in terms of what the user understands. For me, it is also part of my creative process. I often like to look at things in one domain and then transfer that to another domain. Seeing things as blueprint/photocopy takes something in one domain and transfer it to rules for reflow2 (a different domain). Clearly my brother likes things in terms of what they actually are. We've spent many brainstorming tasks in persona/lens, so this might sharpen those decisions about what applying a persona is. Obviously, in the actual design graph, they should be in terms of what they actually are."

WHAT IT SHARPENS:
1. A LENS IS MORE THAN VOCABULARY. The recorded lens so far is about which domain's words a person owns (a baseball coach, a systems engineer). This adds THINKING STYLE: one person reasons by carrying a structure across from another domain and works best when the agent meets them there. Another wants the thing named as what it is and finds an analogy a translation cost. Same design, same facts, opposite best explanations. Neither is recoverable from a job title.
2. THE ANALOGY IS A TOOL FOR THINKING, NOT A NAME FOR THE RECORD. Cross-domain framing is welcome in conversation with a person who works that way. It is how the one-design rules were found. It must be translated at the RECORD BOUNDARY: node names, statements and anything SERVED say what the thing is. This matches where-am-i's standing line ("it shapes how you SPEAK, never what you WRITE INTO the design") and extends it to terms the USER coins, not only to the agent's jargon.
3. WHY THE RECORD HAS ONE REGISTER: a design shared by two readers with opposite styles (Anthony and Alex, dec:idea-two-readers-share-one-design-and-the-session-not-the-graph-says-which-lens-applies) can only hold one register. The literal one serves both; an analogy serves only the person who made it. Measured the same day: the six rules were understood by their author and rewritten by the second reader into two processes in plain words.

OPEN: should a coined analogy that shaped a decision be KEPT beside it, marked as how the idea was reached (useful to its author, and to anyone asking how the rules came about), or dropped once the literal wording lands?

═══ 2026-09-28 — @ajs's LEANING: THE PERSONA LEAVES THE DESIGN. STILL OPEN; he asked "what do you think?" ═══
@ajs, in the dev_reflow2 hub session: "This might be a shift from previous design requirements, but starting to feel that reflow2 should just maintain the pure design and who contributed to it like who:ajs for instance. It is the agent's job to apply the lens and I think flo2 should be what stores it. I think this is a clearer separation of concerns? Then reflow2 isn't in the practice of tracking the persona of every person who may view the design. Let's put that in the responsibility of flo2 and let flo2 provide the agent the design + persona of person viewing it."
flo2's half of the same question is flo2's dec:idea-a-persona-lens-per-person (same date, in flo2's design).

THE AGENT'S READING, given when asked: he is right, and it resolves tensions this design already recorded.
- The record never depends on the reader: req:the-agent-learns-who-it-is-talking-to, clause 3 (accepted) already says the lens "never shapes the record". So a design gains nothing from holding a reader's persona. The persona shapes REPLIES only, which is the agent's job.
- reflow2 never overwrites or deletes history. A persona written into a design stays in that design's history forever, including someone else's shared design after the person has left it. Stored by the host, the person can change or remove it.
- A person who only READS a design (shared, or later public) should not leave a trace in it.
- The host verified who is reading. reflow2 can only guess, from the git author (req:the-agent-says-which-recorded-reader-it-assumes-and-the-lens-names-them).
WHAT STAYS IN THE DESIGN: the Contributor as attribution and authority (who wrote, who approved; the owner's-word rule needs it), and a person's ROLE on this design where it matters. This is the "identity holds the person, the graph holds the role" split flo2 named on 2026-09-19.
WHAT IT COSTS, and must be handled:
(i) reflow2 WITHOUT flo2, i.e. a local store in Claude Code or Grok Build. The "host" is then the agent's own memory of its user. The served lens text would change from "read the Contributor's background; if unknown, ask and record it" to "use the reader profile your host or your own memory gives you; if there is none, follow the person's own vocabulary and ask once".
(ii) It revises ACCEPTED records, which needs @ajs's word:
  - req:the-agent-learns-who-it-is-talking-to: what is owed survives; "the record is updated" moves out of the design;
  - req:the-agent-says-which-recorded-reader-it-assumes-and-the-lens-names-them: built on backgrounds stored in the graph, it would be retired at a host that names the reader and reduced elsewhere;
  - cap:the-agent-asks-who-it-is-talking-to: the where-am-i step;
  - the backgrounds now written into who:ajs and who:alex would move out, leaving attribution.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-09-28 — a reader's persona does not live in the design: reflow2 keeps the design and who contributed, the host (flo2) or the agent's own memory holds the persona, and the agent applies it
properties.rationale: Raised from Alex's field report 2026-08-18, sharpened by Anthony the same day, and REDACTED 2026-08-19 on his instruction after he asked whether Alex would encounter his own stored background by cloning this repo. That question surfaced two things worth keeping: the persona does NOT travel between graphs (verified against tools/reflow2_init.py, and now recorded here because it is an unstated consequence of storing personas on Contributor), and this repository is PUBLIC — so an illustrative example naming a real third party by full name and employer, beside a judgement about his technical ability, was a privacy exposure the design point never required. The name is replaced by the generic description that carries the whole argument. A new counter-argument is added stating that whatever ships must bound what a persona may contain, because the first personas written under this idea already overreached.
